video_title: Why Crypto Keeps Going Up Anyway
gist: Bankless weekly roundup (recorded September 17, 2026) arguing that crypto absorbing two bearish events in one week — the Clarity Act failing a Senate procedural vote by 11 and the Fed hiking to a 3.75%-4% target on a 12-0 vote — without selling off is itself early-bull-market confirmation. The hosts dissect the SEC's same-day 'innovation exemption' for onshore tokenized stocks (KYC/whitelisting plus a 0.25%-of-daily-volume cap), the unresolved hot-economy-vs-debasement debate behind a 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, and a rotation into privacy and mid-cap names (Zcash all-time highs above $1,500, Near at $3 on $30B of confidential intents). They close on options as the next DeFi meta (Derive, Lighter, Hyperliquid), Kraken bringing Hyperliquid perps onshore via HIP-3, and S&P Global acquiring OpenZeppelin.

themes.theme: Bull-market tape: good news up, bad news shrugged off

insights.claim: Crypto prices rose or stayed flat in the same week the Clarity Act died in the Senate and the Fed raised rates, which the Bankless hosts read as the definitional signature of an early bull market: sensitivity to good news and insensitivity to bad news.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Use asymmetric reaction function (not absolute price level) as the regime indicator; if bearish headlines stop producing drawdowns, position for continuation rather than waiting for a clean breakout.
insights.quote: good news is making prices go up and bad news is not mattering

insights.claim: Michael Nato's framework puts Bitcoin's confirmation band between $69.9K (the 200-day moving average) and $80.4K (the 50-week moving average): holding inside it keeps the bull case alive and implies the June 30 low was the cycle low, while a sustained multi-week break above $80.4K would confirm an early bull market.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host), citing Michael Nato
insights.so_what: Gives two hard, testable levels for sizing crypto exposure — add on a sustained weekly close above $80.4K, reassess the thesis on a decisive loss of $69.9K.
insights.quote: So, if we stay from 69.9K to 80.4K, we stay in that band, we should be good to go.

insights.claim: Bitcoin bounced off its 200-week moving average, and a second touch of that line would historically imply a move down toward the high $60Ks (roughly $65K-$66K), a scenario crypto Twitter participants are not positioned for.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host)
insights.so_what: Defines the crowded-positioning downside scenario; a retest of the 200-week around $65K-$66K would be a max-pain outcome worth hedging cheaply rather than ignoring.

insights.claim: Both bearish catalysts of the week were arguably pre-priced — almost nobody in crypto actually expected the Clarity Act to pass, and markets were already discounting rate hikes — evidenced by the fact that QQQ and the S&P did not sell off on the news.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host)
insights.so_what: Tempers the bullish read: resilience may reflect prior discounting rather than genuine new demand, so confirm the regime with follow-through on genuinely unexpected news.
insights.quote: Kind of nice to flush the double bad news of no clarity and rate hike in the same day to be honest.

insights.claim: Zcash printed all-time highs above $1,500 after trading at $1,200 a week earlier, outperforming Bitcoin during the bear market and continuing to outperform now — behavior the hosts call abnormal because Bitcoin normally leads and altcoins follow in early bull phases.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: An altcoin leading Bitcoin breaks the standard cycle template; either the privacy bid is structural or it is the market's high-beta expression of a macro trade — both argue for tracking Zcash as the cycle's momentum bellwether.

insights.claim: Two competing explanations for Zcash's move are that it is pure momentum on no news, driven by its role as 'insurance' on Bitcoin's lack of privacy, or that it is the faster-horse vehicle through which crypto is expressing a view that the Fed hike is actually bullish for the asset class.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Which explanation is right determines the trade's durability — momentum unwinds fast, whereas a macro-expression bid persists as long as the rate narrative does.

insights.claim: Near has facilitated over $30 billion of confidential cross-chain transactions through its confidential intents product and holds roughly $70 million in TVL, with the token near $3 after trading around $2 one to two weeks earlier — still far below its 2021 peak around $30.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Concrete adoption metrics, not just narrative, back the privacy tailwind; Near is a second vehicle for the privacy trade alongside Zcash with a large gap to prior highs.

insights.claim: After 6-12 months in which crypto was a barbell of blue chips and memecoins with a dried-up middle, the mid-cap tier is selectively recovering — not universally, but for tokens with genuine adoption — which the hosts frame as a return of funding for startups and business development work.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: A mid-cap recovery is the classic risk-appetite broadening signal; rotate selectively into adoption-backed mid caps rather than staying barbelled.
insights.quote: the middle of the market, which is people's jobs, that's the startups, that's people doing BD efforts that has just been drying up

themes.theme: Hot economy vs. debasement: the bond market war

insights.claim: The Fed raised its target rate to 3.75%-4% on a unanimous 12-0 FOMC vote under new chair Kevin Warsh, justified explicitly on the grounds that inflation is too high and has been for too long.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host)
insights.so_what: A unanimous hike removes the 'captured Fed' variable from the debasement thesis and re-rates the probability of further tightening into a hot economy.
insights.quote: the plain fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long

insights.claim: Warsh appears to have neutralized political pressure by removing forward guidance and letting Fed governors disagree publicly, diffusing responsibility so no single person owns the hike — and Trump responded not by attacking him but by saying the vote does not matter because the board is hostile, while still insisting US rates should be 1% or less.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: If the new chair can hike without triggering a political war, the Fed-independence discount embedded in gold and Bitcoin may be mispriced to the downside.

insights.claim: Because the Fed hiked unanimously rather than bending to the White House, the evidence for a 'corrupt Fed' driving the debasement trade weakens, which shifts the explanation for rising yields toward a genuinely hot economy rather than currency debasement.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: The distinction matters for positioning: a hot-economy yield rise favors cyclicals and hurts long duration, whereas a debasement yield rise favors gold and Bitcoin.

insights.claim: The US 10-year Treasury yield broke 5% for the first time since roughly 2007-2008 and is trending higher despite Treasury Secretary Bessent buying roughly $6 billion of the long end in a week, an intervention the hosts argue is two orders of magnitude too small to control the market.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Treasury buybacks at current scale are not a credible yield cap; fade the idea that the Treasury is 'the house' unless purchase size increases roughly 100x.
insights.quote: a tiny man going up against the gargantuan barn market

insights.claim: Rising yields may reflect a 1980s-style hot economy — strong nominal GDP plus still-high inflation plus heavy capital demand from AI data-center and infrastructure investment raising the cost of capital — an environment most current investors have never traded in their careers.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host)
insights.so_what: If cost of capital is rising from investment demand rather than money printing, duration-sensitive and debasement-hedge trades underperform real-economy cyclicals.
insights.quote: I think the real reason might just be back to the 1980s, we are in a hot economy.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's simple bull case is framed as path-independent with respect to rates: cutting to zero pushes capital down the risk curve, while raising rates makes government debt service unpayable and forces debasement, so the speaker concludes Bitcoin wins either way and is unbothered by the hike.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: A convenient heads-I-win framing to stress-test: it removes rate direction as a reason to trim Bitcoin, but also means rate moves carry no incremental information for sizing.
insights.quote: So like Bitcoin wins either way.

insights.claim: Tom Lee predicts the S&P 500, at roughly 7,585 at the time of the interview, could easily exceed 8,200 by year-end and that Q4 plus next year could deliver one of the biggest rallies of investors' lifetimes, driven by Mag 7 and software names as long as the AI trade is not extinguished.
insights.speaker: Tom Lee
insights.so_what: An ~8% year-end S&P target from a widely-followed bull, explicitly conditioned on the AI trade surviving the correction — a clean if/then to monitor.
insights.quote: I think we could easily be above 8,200 by the end of the year.

insights.claim: Michael Howell's 'Treasury QE' regime thesis — that the shift from Fed QE to Treasury-driven liquidity provision will be more bullish for Main Street than for Wall Street asset prices — is flagged as an underrated framework the hosts want explored.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host), citing Michael Howell
insights.so_what: If liquidity provision routes through the Treasury into the real economy, the historic reflex of buying financial assets on liquidity expansion may underperform real-economy exposure.

themes.theme: Clarity Act death and the partisan math

insights.claim: The Clarity Act failed a Senate procedural vote on Tuesday, falling 11 votes short of the required supermajority with every Democrat voting no, despite Trump having agreed earlier that week to the updated ethics provision that was billed as the final obstacle.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Legislative crypto market structure is dead for this Congress; base future regulatory expectations on agency rulemaking rather than statute.

insights.claim: News that Trump accepted the ethics provision doubled the Clarity Act's odds on Polymarket and moved Bitcoin from $77K to $79K and ETH from $2,400 to $2,500 before the vote failed.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Quantifies the legislative beta: roughly a 2-3% Bitcoin move per major Clarity headline, a size worth knowing for event-driven positioning on future bills.

insights.claim: Democrats had no incentive to pass the Clarity Act because it would be a purely partisan Republican win with no benefit to their constituents, and they believe they are positioned to win the midterms and can simply wait until they control the House.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Implies no crypto market-structure legislation before the midterms regardless of concessions offered — stop pricing near-term legislative catalysts.

insights.claim: The ethics concessions were forward-looking only and did not touch the roughly $1.4 billion of prior Trump-family crypto dealings, meaning the Trump side gave up nothing of value — and the co-host argues Trump's own crypto dealings are the single biggest reason the Clarity Act failed.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Reframes the blockage as conflict-of-interest risk rather than partisan obstruction, which means it persists as long as the Trump family retains crypto exposure.
insights.quote: Donald Trump is the biggest reason why Clarity Act did not pass.

insights.claim: With legislation dead, SEC chair Paul Atkins and CFTC chairman Mike Selig signaled they will act within existing statutory authority, and the industry argument is that the durable defense against a hostile future administration is adoption rather than law — the Uber and Airbnb playbook.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host), citing Paul Atkins, Mike Selig and an industry commentator
insights.so_what: The regulatory toolkit to watch is exemptive relief, no-action letters, registration pathways and rulemaking — faster but more reversible than statute, so track adoption metrics as the real moat.
insights.quote: Adoption is now the mandate for the industry.

insights.claim: A commentator argues that politicians who blocked the Clarity Act will regret it because unconstrained regulators will push crypto integration further and faster than the bill would have, making the legislation the more conservative option.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host), citing Nick
insights.so_what: Inverts the standard read of the vote as a crypto loss; expect a faster, less bounded regulatory expansion than a statute would have permitted.
insights.quote: I think there are a number of politicians who are going to wish they passed Clarity Act by the time regulators are done pushing crypto forward.

themes.theme: SEC innovation exemption: onshore tokenized stocks

insights.claim: Roughly 21 hours after the Clarity Act vote failed, the SEC released an 'innovation exemption' effective immediately that lets true one-to-one tokenized stocks with KYC and whitelisting trade on AMMs and DEXes on public permissionless blockchains, and explicitly treats venues like Uniswap and Aerodrome as trading venues rather than exchanges or broker-dealers.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: First US regulatory carve-out removing broker-dealer classification risk from DEX front ends — a structural de-risking for DEX protocol tokens and onshore RWA infrastructure.

insights.claim: The exemption imposes a hard cap of 0.25% of an asset's daily trading volume on chain, so an equity trading 1,000 shares per day in public markets could only support 25 tokenized shares of daily on-chain volume, which rules out institutional size and confines the regime to a small retail sandbox.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host) and Ryan (Bankless host)
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite onshore tokenized-equity volume forecasts against real equity markets; revenue from this channel is capped at a fraction of a percent until the cap is lifted.

insights.claim: Securitize's publicly traded stock rose roughly 30% on the day of the SEC announcement because its business is true one-to-one tokenization of real equity, not just economic rights, making it the clearest beneficiary among Coinbase, Dinari, Robinhood and Ondo.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: The market has already picked its winner from the exemption; use Securitize's reaction as the read-through benchmark for pricing other tokenization names.

insights.claim: The exemption requires that smart contracts be auditable, public and deployed on a public permissionless distributed ledger, which implies walled-garden chains without a distributed validator base would fail the test — leaving single-sequencer L2s, Base and Robinhood Chain in an unresolved gray area the SEC did not define.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Chain-level eligibility becomes a regulatory moat; if single-sequencer chains are excluded, tokenized-equity liquidity concentrates on the most credibly decentralized chains.
insights.quote: Smart contracts must be auditable, public, and deployed on a public permissionless distributed ledger

insights.claim: The co-host argues the KYC'd, whitelisted onshore tokenized equity is a strictly inferior product to the existing offshore permissionless versions because it sacrifices permissionlessness and global access, predicting user preference will stay offshore even as the onshore product gains legitimacy.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Legitimacy does not equal volume; offshore tokenized equity venues may keep winning flow, which matters for where fee revenue actually accrues.
insights.quote: the KYC onore compliant ones are strictly an inferior product

insights.claim: The SEC-exempted tokens carry full shareholder governance and economic rights including voting, which directly answers the AMC CEO's stated objection to Robinhood's tokenized shares — and Robinhood's Vlad has said the offshore Robinhood stock tokens will also add in-kind redemption and voting.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Tokenized equities are converging on feature parity with real shares except for KYC, removing the governance-rights objection that has been the main public attack line.
insights.quote: there's no way an actual company with shareholders wants token holder shareholder votes in the hand of some hacker from North Korea

insights.claim: The CFTC is reportedly permitting developers to build passive derivative software, including for crypto markets, without registering as brokers, and the SEC is separately convening a round table with crypto and TradFi participants on 24/7 trading market structure.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Two more agency-level tailwinds arriving without legislation; 24/7 equity trading would be a direct structural win for on-chain venues.

themes.theme: Options as the next DeFi meta

insights.claim: Options are framed as the last major derivative crypto has failed to productize despite a graveyard of failed startups, and the argument for why this time differs is that options need a large, diverse set of market participants with opposing directional views, which crypto lacked when it was just concentrated retail plus crypto-native funds.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host), citing Nick of Derive
insights.so_what: Participant diversity, not technology, is the gating variable for options product-market fit — a testable precondition to monitor before allocating to options protocols.
insights.quote: there has been a graveyard of startups trying to build options in crypto

insights.claim: The 10/10 liquidation event demonstrated that perpetuals carry risk encumbrance options do not: a perp trader can be directionally right and still be liquidated by volatility, whereas an option holder who picks asset, strike and expiry cannot be liquidated before expiry and is also insulated from platform contagion and auto-deleveraging.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host), citing Nick of Derive
insights.so_what: Post-crash demand should rotate from perps toward defined-risk options structures; watch options open interest as the tell for whether this substitution is actually happening.
insights.quote: with a perpetual, you can be directionally right, but still get liquidated due to volatility

insights.claim: The Derive token rose roughly 150% in the past month and 50% in the past two weeks, and Derive already dominates HYPE options volume as the most liquid venue for them, setting up a three-way race against Lighter and Hyperliquid for the options meta.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Named as a 'starting pistol' for a sector rotation into options protocols that could run for the rest of the year; Derive is the incumbent, Hyperliquid and Lighter the challengers.

themes.theme: Onshore perps, token value accrual and consolidation

insights.claim: Kraken is bringing Hyperliquid perpetuals to onshore US users through a compliant KYC-permissioned HIP-3 marketplace, letting US citizens and entities trade perps that route through Hyperliquid with Kraken as the front end — and the hosts distinguish this from the Lighter-Robinhood tie-up, which sits in the Robinhood wallet app rather than the core exchange.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Licensed exchange front ends over permissionless perp backends is the emerging template for onshore access; it channels US retail perp flow into Hyperliquid's fee base.

insights.claim: AI token consumption on Venice is doubling roughly every two months, going from about 50 billion tokens per day six months ago to about 250 billion per day now, and because VVV value capture maps close to one-to-one with token consumption, continued acceleration implies a repricing of VVV.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host), citing Erik Voorhees's chart
insights.so_what: A rare directly modelable crypto-AI revenue curve: track daily inference token consumption as the leading indicator for VVV's fundamental value.

insights.claim: The hosts argue the asset class needs a dozen or two dozen clear successes of value-accrual tokens — naming VVV, HYPE and LIT, and citing a model of using 25% of protocol fees to buy the token — to break the market's assumption that all tokens are uninvestable lemons.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: Use fee-to-buyback mechanics as the screen for the next cycle's leadership; the hosts believe a critical mass of such successes is the precondition for broad altcoin re-rating.
insights.quote: we have to make tokens investable again

insights.claim: Arc Chain launched with roughly 100 memecoin launchpads on day one, which the co-host reads as a decision to compete in the alt-L1 landscape rather than take the payments and e-commerce integration path, a positioning he argues is wrong because USDC is backend bank plumbing without Robinhood-style front-end distribution.
insights.speaker: David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: A bearish read on a high-profile stablecoin-issuer chain launch; the counterargument offered is that memecoin speculation is just early bootstrapping for later payments and tokenized-asset plumbing.
insights.quote: I don't think they should be competing there at all. That is not their arena.

insights.claim: S&P Global acquired OpenZeppelin, one of crypto's oldest and most prominent smart contract auditing and engineering firms, for an undisclosed sum, with OpenZeppelin-associated contracts having handled $37 trillion in value transferred.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Bankless host) and David (Bankless co-host)
insights.so_what: TradFi data and ratings incumbents are buying crypto security infrastructure outright — a signal that on-chain audit and risk assessment is becoming a ratings-agency business line.
